summary: Menus that stop at the window edge and scroll, copy from a fence as plain text, one scrollbar thumb, bars that fade when the pointer leaves the window, and highlights in Apple's system colours.
new: `markdown::highlight_solid` answers a `HighlightColor` at full strength, Apple's system colour for the appearance, for a picker's swatch.
changed: `menu::card` takes `&mut Window` before `cx`. Every menu panel, root or submenu, is capped at the window's height less the snap margin either side and scrolls its rows past that, with the overlay scrollbar. The keyboard's row is kept in view, and a submenu hangs off its row wherever the row has scrolled to.
`markdown::default_highlight` paints `highlight_solid` at 0.32 on dark and 0.45 on light, keeping text at 7:1 or better.
Every scrollbar thumb is 4px wide; `Overlay` and `Viewport` bars were 6px.
fixed: Copy and cut inside a fence, which is the whole of `Mode::Source`, put the selected text on the clipboard as it stands rather than wrapped in a fence. A selection spanning a fence and the blocks around it still copies as markdown.
A transient scrollbar (`Overlay`, `Viewport`, `VariableList`) fades after the pointer leaves the window across its track instead of staying raised.

summary: The shell's working directory from the shell itself, and a client-decorated window that keeps its frame clear across an appearance switch.
new: `Emulator::directory` answers the working directory the shell last reported through `OSC 7 ; file://host/path` or `OSC 9 ; 9 ; path`: percent-decoded, the host dropped, a Windows `/C:/` path without its leading slash, and the quotes around a `9 ; 9` path taken off. `None` until a report arrives; a shell that sends neither never sets it. `scanner::Segment::Directory` carries the report.
fixed: `appearance::reapply_window_background` pushes `Transparent` rather than `Opaque` onto a window under `Decorations::Client`, so a switch between light and dark no longer fills the corners and resize band `ui::window::frame` leaves clear.

summary: Reader highlights in five colours, anchors that find their words again after an outside edit, pictures that resolve against their document, a page frame that takes presses and drags for the editor, and a paste into source that lands in the source.
new: `markdown::Editing::base` names the directory a relative image path is joined onto, and `markdown::image_source` resolves a URL the way the renderer does: anything with `://` and any absolute path as written, a relative path under the base. The editor takes one per document through `Editor::with_base`, `set_base` and `base`. The stored URL is unchanged.

`Editor::press` takes a press from a host frame around the editor — padding, a floor under a short document — and places the caret at the nearest row, starts a drag, or dismisses a selection, as a press on the document would. A press the editor's own box took is marked with `Window::prevent_default` and ignored.

`markdown::HighlightColor` names a reader's highlight — yellow, green, blue, pink, purple — with a stable `name` to store and `from_name` to read it back. `Annotation::Highlight(color)` washes an anchor's range in it, so an editor anchor can be a highlight as well as a comment thread.

`markdown::set_highlight_paint` installs what each `HighlightColor` paints, handed the theme so light and dark can differ. Without it, `markdown::default_highlight` paints a translucent wash that keeps text at 7:1 or better.

`markdown::Quote` finds a range again in a document changed outside the editor. `Quote::of` takes the text under a range and up to 32 characters either side; `Quote::find` answers the saved range while it still covers that text, and otherwise the occurrence with the most context intact, nearest the old position on a tie.

`ToggleHighlight`, on `cmd-shift-h` on macOS and `ctrl-shift-h` elsewhere, toggles the custom mark named `editor::HIGHLIGHT_MARK` (`highlight`) and does nothing until the app registers a mark under that name.
changed: `markdown::Editing` has a `base` field; a struct literal without `..Default::default()` has to name it.
`ImageStore::keep` takes the asking editor's base as a third argument, `Option<&Path>`. The store runs while that editor is being updated, and reading it there panics.
Editor anchors are no longer comment-only: `CommentId` is `AnchorId`, `EditorEvent::CommentActivated` is `EditorEvent::AnchorActivated`, and `Editor::comment_at` is `Editor::anchor_at`.
`markdown::Annotation` is `#[non_exhaustive]`.
fixed: A file dragged over the editor and taken out or released elsewhere no longer leaves the drop line behind.
A text selection, a lifted block and an image resize keep following the pointer once a drag leaves the editor's box.

Paste in source mode, or inside a code block, inserts the clipboard text at the caret and leaves the caret after it, rather than splicing parsed blocks in beside the source. A URL, a picture or a copied file goes in as its text there.

summary: The rest of the kitty graphics protocol, sixel and iTerm2 images, and a terminal that answers the pixel size queries programs probe with before they send one.
new: The terminal answers `CSI 14 t` and `CSI 16 t` from the cell size `Emulator::set_cell_size` measured, and every reply leaves in the order its query arrived.

Kitty placements by id: `a=p` places a stored image, `p` names a placement so one image can hold several, and `I` transmits and names an image by number, echoed in the reply. Every delete carries out its target — `a`, `i`, `n`, `c`, `p`, `q`, `x`, `y`, `z`, `r` — and an upper-case one frees the data of each image it leaves with no placement.

Kitty display keys: `z` layers an image over the text, under it, or under non-default cell backgrounds; `x`, `y`, `w`, `h` crop the source; `X`, `Y` offset it inside its first cell; `c` or `r` alone scales by the image's aspect, and both letterbox it.
Kitty payloads compressed with zlib (`o=z`), inflated whole and held to the same 64 MiB ceiling as an uncompressed one.
Kitty Unicode placeholders: a virtual placement (`U=1`) is shown wherever the text holds `U+10EEEE` cells naming it, which is the path multiplexers take. `kitty::PLACEHOLDER` is the character.

Kitty file, temporary file and shared memory transmission (`t=f`, `t=t`, `t=s`, with `O` and `S`), off until a host calls `Emulator::set_local_media(true)`. Paths resolve through symlinks, `/proc`, `/sys` and `/dev` are refused, only regular files are read, and every failure is the one `EBADF` reply.

Kitty relative placements (`P`, `Q`, `H`, `V`), found from their parent each frame and deleted with it, refused with `ENOPARENT`, `ECYCLE`, `ETOODEEP` past a chain of eight, or `EINVAL` for a virtual one.

Kitty animation: `a=f` adds or edits a frame over a blank, colored or earlier canvas, `a=a` sets the state, current frame, loop count and gaps, `a=c` composes a rectangle of one frame onto another, and `d=f` deletes a frame. `view::Images` plays them and schedules a repaint for when the next frame is due.

Sixel images, placed at the cursor the way `a=T` places a kitty image. `Emulator::set_advertise_sixel(true)` answers DA1 as `CSI ? 62 ; 4 ; 22 c` for programs that look for sixel there before sending one.
iTerm2 inline images (`OSC 1337 ; File=`), sent whole or in parts between `MultipartFile` and `FileEnd`, sized in cells, pixels or percent, with `preserveAspectRatio`. An animated GIF plays.
changed: `terminal::scanner` holds `Scanner`, `Segment` and the new `Iterm`, which were in `kitty`. `Segment` reports sixel data, iTerm2 files and `CSI 16 t` alongside kitty commands and mode 2026.

`Segment`, `Iterm`, `kitty::Action`, `kitty::Target`, `kitty::Effect`, `kitty::Command`, `kitty::Display`, `kitty::Reply`, `kitty::Delete`, `emulator::Placement` and `view::PlacedImage` are `#[non_exhaustive]`.

`kitty::Store::apply` answers an `Effect` — a placement or a delete for the emulator to carry out — rather than a `Display`, and `kitty::Reply` is a struct carrying the `I` and `p` it echoes. `Command::compressed` is `Command::compression`.

`emulator::Placement` carries the placement's `frame`, `source` and `z`. `view::PlacedImage` carries them too, with `id`, `frame_index`, `next_frame` and `wake`; its `image` is the one frame to paint.
A lower-case `d=a` or `d=i` takes placements off the screen and keeps the image data, so the image can be placed again; the upper-case form frees it.
An image of the default z-index paints over the text rather than under it, as the protocol has it.
New dependencies: `miniz_oxide`, already in the tree under `png`, and `libc` on unix.
fixed: Several placements can share one top-left cell; placing a second one there no longer drops the first.
`a=q` answers what the same transmission would — a refused medium, an unreadable file, a payload that does not fit its size — and stores nothing.

summary: A window that closes without taking the app with it, a caret that holds its column through a scroll, and a key for either end of the document.
new: The editor moves the caret to the start and end of the document with `cmd-up` and `cmd-down` on macOS and `ctrl-home` and `ctrl-end` elsewhere, and selects to them with shift held. The actions are `DocumentStart`, `DocumentEnd`, `SelectDocumentStart` and `SelectDocumentEnd`.
changed: bezel-gpui 0.3.12.
fixed: Closing a window on macOS no longer crashes the app. zed-industries/zed#64143 drops the accessibility adapter when a window is dropped, which restores the content view's class and discards the KVO subclass AppKit's touch bar finder installed to observe `nextResponder`; the finder then removed that observation during the next display-cycle flush and raised `NSRangeException`. bezel-gpui 0.3.12 flushes the display cycle before dropping the adapter.

Up and down keep the caret on its row when the move scrolls the editor. The row a run of vertical moves holds is measured from the caret rather than the window, so a scroll between two presses no longer sends the next one to the wrong line.

Up and down land on the painted position nearest the column they started in, on the row they were aiming for. A soft-wrapped line is hit tested one row at a time rather than as a whole paragraph at the row's middle.
Typing, select all, undo and redo end a run of vertical moves, so the next up or down starts from where the caret is rather than a column held from before.
The goal column survives a trip to either end of the document: moving up from the first line or down from the last and then back returns the caret to the column it came from.

summary: The pointer reported to the programs that ask for it, a frame held whole through a synchronized update, and kitty images that stay where they were put.
new: `Emulator::mouse_mode` is what the running program wants done with the pointer — `MouseTracking` for `1000`, `1002` and `1003`, the `1006` and `1005` encodings, `1007` alternate scroll, and the alternate screen and DECCKM those last two read. `view::mouse_bytes` turns a `MouseAction` and a cell into the report the program is waiting for, and answers `None` where the event is the user's, which is the host's signal to run its own selection or scrollback instead. SGR names the button that came up and carries a grid past 223 columns; the original encoding numbers every release 3 and declines a cell it cannot name rather than reporting the wrong one. Alt and control travel on a report, and shift never does: it is how a user reaches the selection under a program holding the pointer.

`Emulator::render_hold` is a program asking for the screen to stop updating (mode 2026). While it is on, `lines`, `line`, `cursor` and `placements` serve the grid as it stood when the mode went on — the frame the program means to leave on screen, since nothing after the sequence that began the hold had been folded in yet. A selection made during one still washes, because a hold stops output rather than the pointer. The emulator has no clock and never ends a hold itself: `Emulator::release_hold` and `emulator::HOLD_TIMEOUT` are what a host arms so a program that dies mid-frame cannot freeze the grid. A resize ends one.

`kitty::Display` carries a display command's `c`, `r` and `C` keys, which is what `Store::apply` now answers an `a=T` with. `c` and `r` state the cell extent outright in place of the image's own pixels against the measured cell, and `C=1` reserves no rows and moves no cursor — an image drawn over whatever is already there, which is what a program positioning its own frame wants.

The kitty keyboard protocol. `Emulator::keyboard_mode` reads back the flags a program pushed — `alacritty_terminal` keeps the mode stack, the alternate-screen swap and the `CSI ? u` query reply, all of which now run because the terminal is built with `kitty_keyboard` on. `view::keystroke_bytes` encodes against them: flag 1 takes `Esc` and the control and alt combos to `CSI <code>;<modifiers>u` and leaves every other key on its legacy encoding, flag 8 takes the text keys as well, flag 2 hangs a press, repeat or release off the modifier as a subparameter, and flag 16 carries the text the key produced. `F3` moves to `CSI 13~`, its legacy `CSI 1;<mod>R` being a cursor position report. Flag 4 carries the shifted key in the first parameter's second subparameter, where shift is held. The base layout key is not served: gpui reports the active layout only.
changed: `kitty::Store::apply` answers `Option<kitty::Display>` in place of `Option<u32>`. The image id is `Display::image`.

A placement anchors every cell of its top row rather than only its top-left, so text written over the left of an image leaves it where it was instead of taking it off the grid. Displaying an image takes its earlier placements with it, which is what keeps a program redrawing a frame to one placement per image.

`view::keystroke_bytes` takes an `emulator::KeyboardMode` in place of the `app_cursor` flag, which is now a field on it, a `view::KeyEvent` saying whether the key was pressed, held or let go, and the `gpui::KeyLayout` the platform reported for the press. gpui folds a shifted key into `Keystroke::key` for everything but `a`-`z` and clears `Modifiers::shift` with it, so `shift-1` arrives as `!` with no shift held; the kitty encoding reads the unshifted key and the shift bit off the layout, and the legacy encoding keeps using the folded key, which is the text that was typed. A host with no key-up path passes `KeyEvent::Press`, and one whose platform reports no layout passes `None`; `Emulator::keyboard_mode` fills the rest.
bezel-gpui 0.3.11, which is the release that reports `KeyLayout`.
fixed: Light glass shows the backdrop it refracts. Light `glass_regular` was the measured material verbatim — gain 0.139 under a white tint at 214/255, which is 84% tint — and over a real blur a popover read as a white sheet with whatever sat behind it ghosting through. It now trades a third of that tint for gain (0.40 at 150/255), holding the `tint.a / (1 - gain)` product `SurfaceSpec::flat` reads so a build with no lens keeps the white panel it had; saturation comes down to 2.2 with it, 4.27 having been fit at 13.9% transmission. `Theme::glass_overlay` and `Theme::card_glass_bg` cover 0.55 and 0.60 in light where they covered 0.85.

A kitty image inside a synchronized update no longer lands under the frame's own text. `vte` buffers mode 2026 and replays it at ESU, and graphics leave the stream ahead of that buffer, so the image was placed against the cursor the frame had not moved yet and the replay then wrote over its anchor. `emulator::NoSync` turns the buffering off — every byte now reaches the grid in the order the program wrote it — and the frame is held in the emulator instead.

A named key held with a modifier now states it as a CSI parameter: `ctrl-left` is `CSI 1;5D` and `shift-delete` is `CSI 3;2~`. Ctrl with a named key used to encode nothing at all, since caret notation has no byte for one, and shift with an arrow sent the arrow alone. A modifier also rules out the SS3 form, which has nowhere to put the parameter, so a modified arrow is CSI whatever DECCKM is set to.

summary: Images on the grid where a client sends them, a menu panel that picks the side with room, and a result list with a bottom.
new: `terminal::kitty` is the graphics protocol, taken off the stream ahead of the parser. `vte` routes an APC run into a discard state and offers `Perform` no hook to catch it, so `kitty::Scanner` splits those runs out first and hands the rest on to `alacritty_terminal` unchanged, in order. It holds its state across feeds, since a pty read ends wherever the kernel filled the buffer.

`kitty::Store` assembles a chunked transmission under its id and holds 64 images of up to 64 MiB each, oldest dropped. `a=t`, `a=T`, `a=q` and `a=d` by id or all; `f=24`, `f=32` and `f=100`. Direct transmission only — a file, a temp file, shared memory and `o=z` compression are answered `ENOTSUPPORTED` rather than left unanswered, which is what keeps a client from waiting on a reply that never comes. `q=1` and `q=2` are read off the chunk that stated the transmission's keys, not the one that ended it.

`Emulator::placements` is where the images on the visible grid sit, in cells. Each anchors on a private-use zerowidth char written onto its top-left cell, so it rides the grid's own scroll, scrollback and reflow: `alacritty_terminal` exposes no absolute line number and no scroll callback, and a side table keyed by line drifts the first time output scrolls. `Emulator::set_cell_size` is what turns an image's pixels into rows and columns, and an image that arrives before the first frame is stored unplaced until one does. `Emulator::selection_text` drops the anchors, so copying across an image pastes no character nobody can see.

`view::Images` decodes what the store holds into the BGRA frames gpui paints and caches them across frames, keyed by the client's id; `GridSnapshot::images` carries them to `TerminalElement`, which paints each over the cell backgrounds and under the glyphs — where kitty puts an image of the default z-index.

`scroll::Beyond` is what lies past a drifting pane's edge, and so whether a pointer carried out there is still aiming at the pane. `Nothing` holds full speed for as long as the pointer is outside, which is a board that fills the window; `Neighbour` stops at the edge, because what the pointer is over now belongs to somebody else. `scroll::pane_velocity` is the ramp for both axes on its own, above `drift_velocity`.

`scroll::Viewport::track_scroll` hands a viewport a `ScrollHandle` of the caller's — what `ScrollHandle::scroll_to_item` needs to reach one of its children. Left unset the viewport keeps a handle of its own, as before.

A searchable picker's result list shows twelve rows and scrolls past that, so a palette over hundreds of commands opens the same size as one over twenty. The query line stays above the scroller, since it is what the rows are an answer to. The arrows scroll the highlighted row into view — following the selection rather than leading it, so a wheel stays the reader's — and a new query returns the list to the top. `CommandPalette` and `Combobox` both.

`popover::submenu::place` fits a panel beside a rectangle rather than around gpui's point: a submenu opens to the right of the card it hangs on, or to its left where the window has no room on the right, and slides vertically the way every menu does. `popover::Chain` is the side one open tree settled on, shared by every panel in it — a panel that had to flip is one whose children have no room to the right either, and a deeper panel deciding alone would open back across its parent.
changed: `scroll::drift` takes a `scroll::Beyond`. Pass `Beyond::Nothing` for what it did before.

`GridSnapshot` carries an `images` field. A host that never shows graphics adds `images: Vec::new()`; one that does holds a `view::Images` beside its emulator, calls `Emulator::set_cell_size` from the grid hook with the metrics it is handed, and fills the field from `Images::placed`.

`popover::anchored_submenu` takes the open menu's `popover::Chain` and mounts on a row that is `relative()` — the row is what it measures the parent card's edges from. `menu::card` passes its own, one per render; a caller driving panels by hand holds one the same way.
fixed: A submenu near the window's right edge no longer opens across the card that dropped it. gpui's `anchored` fits a layer to the window around a point, and the point here was the parent card's own right edge: snapping slid the panel left over the card, and `SwitchAnchor` mirrored it about that edge onto almost exactly the same place. A submenu has to clear a rectangle, which is what `popover::submenu::place` works from.

summary: The window chrome a platform without a titlebar hands over: a frame where the compositor draws none, caption buttons where the desktop puts them, and a bar that drags by its grip.
new: `ui::window::frame` wraps an app's root in the frame its window owes — a border, `Theme::surface_radius` corners, a shadow, and a `Theme::CLIENT_INSET` band that resizes from all eight directions. It reads `Window::window_decorations` per frame: under `Decorations::Server` the child comes back untouched, which is macOS, Windows, X11 and KDE. GNOME's Wayland session has never implemented `xdg-decoration` and answers `Client` whatever was asked for, and that is the case this paints. An edge `tiling` reports flush keeps its square corner and gives up its band.

`ui::window::resize_edge` is which edge a press resizes, or `None` for a press on the content. The corners take their `inset` square and the edges take what is left between them, so the hitboxes the frame lays down need no order between them.

`titlebar::controls` is the caption cluster off macOS — minimize, maximize or restore, and close. Call it at both ends of the bar with `CaptionSide` and the desktop decides which end fills: `App::button_layout` reads GNOME's `gtk-decoration-layout`, and a platform reporting no layout puts the three on the right. Empty in full screen, and short whatever `Window::window_controls` says the compositor refuses.
`titlebar::grip` is the bare stretch of a bar that moves its window, zooms it on a double click and opens the desktop's window menu on a right press. It takes the free space the content leaves.

`keys::printed` writes a chord nothing is bound to the way the platform writes it — `secondary-s` is `⌘S` against `Ctrl+S`, while `cmd-s`, `super-s` and `win-s` name the platform key itself and print `⌘S` against `Win+S`. For a label naming a chord the keymap does not own; where there is a binding, `keys::shortcut` cannot drift and this can.
`Theme::CLIENT_INSET` is the band a client-decorated window keeps outside its content, and `Theme::CAPTION_BUTTON_WIDTH` one caption button.
`ui::stats` reads CPU time and memory on Windows, through `GetProcessTimes` and `GetProcessMemoryInfo`. Both were blank there.
changed: `titlebar::titlebar` no longer moves the window and no longer takes a `DragState` — put a `titlebar::grip` in the bar and give it the state instead. The bar used to be one `WindowControlArea::Drag`, which is how Windows answers `WM_NCHITTEST`, and the platform takes the first control area the pointer falls in: every interactive child then had to `occlude()` to stay clickable, and occluding takes the scroll wheel from everything behind it. Naming the drag surface costs the controls nothing.
The default mono face on Windows is Cascadia Mono, which ships with Windows 11 and with Terminal, in place of Consolas.
`ctrl-y` redoes off macOS, beside `ctrl-shift-z`, in both the text field and the editor keymaps.
`bezel-ui` turns on a fourth `bezel-icons` category, `shapes`, for the square a caption button maximizes with. Cargo unions features, so it is the floor for anything depending on `ui`.
fixed: `ctrl-shift-c` in a terminal view no longer sends `ETX`. It was reaching the control-byte table, so copying interrupted the foreground process; it and `ctrl-shift-v` now fall through for the app to bind, and `ctrl-c` stays SIGINT.

summary: A checkbox you can click, and tabs that open and close with their order held apart from their paint.
new: A press on a task block's checkbox checks it. `Editor::toggle_task` is the same entry point, one undo step, and it leaves the caret where it was — a press in the gutter beside the box still places one.
`BlockLayouts::checkbox_bounds` is where a task block's box painted, for a host hit-testing its own press.

`Editing::toggle` makes the box a control and says who answers the press. `Toggle::Handled` has the box take the press and hand over the block it belongs to, for a document rendered without an editor; `Toggle::HitTested` paints it as a control and leaves the press to a caller resolving it against `BlockLayouts::checkbox_bounds`, which is what the editor does. Unset paints a marker.
`Editing::copy` is whether a fence paints its copy button. `CopyButton::Hidden` with no `toggle` is a document holding no listener at all.

`markdown::parse_ranges` returns a `ParsedDoc` — the document, and the source range each block was parsed from. The ranges partition the source, so an app can re-serialize the blocks it edited and splice the rest back byte for byte rather than writing the whole file out in canonical form.

`ui::tabs::Strip` is a tab order and the one in front — `open`, `close`, `activate`, `cycle` and `reorder` — with no gpui in it, so what a close hands over to and where a cycle wraps are tested without a window.
`ui::tabs::bar`, `tab` and `close` paint the strip: a row that scrolls once its tabs stop fitting, a label carrying an optional glyph, mark and badge, and a `×` on show or behind the hover.
`tabs::Label::mark` is a glyph beside the name — unsaved work, a running job, something unread. `ui` names none itself, so the category a mark comes from stays the app's to pay for.

Every `tabs::tab` but a `State::Focused` one washes on hover, a `Front` tab in a background pane included. It takes that hover itself, so chaining `.hover(..)` on hits gpui's panic on a second — reach for a `group_hover`.

A `&str` converts to a `Doc` or a `ParsedDoc`, `(source, &marks)` to a `Doc`, a `&Doc` to a `String`, a `BlockKind` to a `Block` at the left margin, a `String` or `&str` to unmarked `Text`, and a `Cursor` to the collapsed `Selection` around it. Each is the `From` for the call it already had — `parse`, `parse_with`, `parse_ranges`, `serialize`, `Block::new`, `Text::plain`, `Selection::at`. Serializing with marks has no `From`: `String` is foreign and a tuple is not a local type.
`Controls::toggle_group_icon` is a segment carrying a glyph rather than a word, at the height a labelled segment takes.

`theme::frosted_window` is whether the compositor puts a backdrop behind a translucent window, and `theme::LENSED` whether this build carries the backdrop-blur primitive. Windows 11 answers the first and not the second, so an app that reads one for the other gets a card it can see through.
changed: An unselected `toggle_group_item` washes on hover. A caller that chained its own `.hover(..)` onto one now hits gpui's panic on a second hover — reach for a `group_hover` instead.

`Vibrancy::Auto` frosts a dark window on Windows 11 build 22621 and up, where `Theme::window_background_appearance` asks for Mica rather than the accent API's acrylic — which is applied at a zero tint and reads as plain transparency. Below that build the backdrop call is a no-op, so the build is read at runtime.
`Theme::VIBRANCY_ALPHA` is 0.80 on every platform. It is the tint's coverage; whether a window frosts at all is now `theme::frosted_window`.

`Brand::default().glass` follows `theme::LENSED`. A Mica window carries no glass: the backdrop is DWM's and the blur a card lays over the content it covers is the renderer's, which on Windows is DirectX and has no such primitive.
fixed: A surface where no lens runs — Windows, Linux, and macOS with glass off — fills with `SurfaceSpec::flat`, the tone its look settles on, instead of the tint alone. The tint is a coverage over a blur; painted flat it covered nothing, and the text behind a composer read straight through the pill.

summary: GFM alerts are a quote kind, and a wrapped row is highlighted from its first glyph.
new: `markdown::QuoteKind` is the GFM alert a blockquote opens with — `[!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`, `[!IMPORTANT]`, `[!WARNING]` and `[!CAUTION]` survive a round trip rather than being escaped to `> \[!TIP\]`.
Typing the last underscore of `__bold__` makes it bold, as the last star of `**bold**` already did.
changed: `BlockKind::Quote(Text)` is now `BlockKind::Quote { kind, text }`; a plain blockquote is `kind: None`.
fixed: Every row of a selection across a soft wrap is covered from its first glyph, and so is anything else painted from a byte range — search and comment highlights, inline-code and chip backgrounds.
Typing `**bold**` one key at a time no longer goes italic at `**bold*`, leaving a stray star behind.

summary: A pane names the room its scrollbar sits in, fields hold a case, and nested panes keep the wheel.
new: `Overlay::channel` centres a bar in room the pane reserves beside its content, in place of the strip at the edge; `scroll::rail_fits` says whether a hand-rolled rail has the room to paint.

A text field holds its text in a `Case`: `with_case`, `set_case` and `case`, applied to every edit rather than to the string on its way out, so what is painted and what `content()` returns are one string.
`scroll::claiming_pane` and `scroll::contain_wheel` keep a capped pane's wheel to itself, and `floating::layer` gives a floating surface a layer of its own.
changed: `scroll::BAR_INSET` and `scroll::RAIL_ROOM` are no longer public: a pane names where its bar sits through `Overlay::channel`, and `scroll::rail_fits` answers what `RAIL_ROOM` was read for.
fixed: A nested pane scrolled past its end no longer carries the wheel into the pane behind it.
A floating layer occludes what sits under it, and the press that dismisses a menu or popover is swallowed rather than reaching the content behind.

summary: Runtime syntax providers, Wasm grammars, and richer text and list controls.
new: Syntax supports runtime language registration, language injections, and optional Wasm grammars with per-session query compilation.
Text fields accept syntax spans and live typography updates; selectable Markdown gains reusable focus and copy handling.
Variable-height virtual lists preserve scroll anchors, follow the tail, and report visible rows.
changed: Linked grammars move to `bezel-syntax-std`; consumers must install a provider or register their own languages.
Tree-sitter moves to 0.27 and the minimum Rust version rises to 1.90.
fixed: Terminal tab markers no longer expand twice during text shaping.
The gallery installs its syntax provider for native highlighting and generated browser samples.
Variable-height list scrollbars honour `Visibility::Scrolling`: the thumb fades after the idle window unless it is being dragged.

summary: Canvas editing respects locks and zoom limits, with faster undo and cached containment.
new: `CanvasEditor::take_events` lets headless callers drain pending events and release retained changes; the view drains them automatically.
changed: Undo batches are built in linear time without repeated vector prepends, preserving undo and redo order.
Rendering and gestures reuse containment indexes for the document and preview, invalidated by edits, measurements and kind changes. Container depths are memoized, including cycles.
`CanvasEditor::selected` finds the primary selection without allocating a temporary vector.
fixed: Zero or negative snap grid spacing paints no dots instead of hanging rendering.
Dragging a selection leaves nodes that disallow dragging stationary and selected.
`fit` and `zoom_to_selection` respect both configured zoom limits.

summary: The canvas edits a graph, with trees as a layer over it, laid out the way an app picks.
new: `CanvasEditor::fit` (`shift-1`) zooms the whole document into view and `zoom_to_selection` (`shift-2`) the selection; a node a key moves to is panned into view, and a drag held near the view's edge pans it. `visible` and `center_on` read and move the part in view.

`CanvasView::with_snap(Snap { grid, guides })` lands dragged and resized boxes on a grid, drawn as dots, and on the edges and middles other nodes share, drawn as guides, through the pure `snap::settle`.
`canvas::minimap(&view, cx)` maps the whole canvas with the part in view outlined; press or drag in it to look there.

Large canvases stay quick: layout indexes the trees once and measures each branch once, edges out of view are not drawn, text is parsed only when it changes, and below 40% a node paints as its box. Two thousand nodes lay out and paint within the tests' bounds.

A node is a container its kind fills: the canvas owns the box, and a kind's render paints everything inside it from a `kind::Look`, the zoom and the in-place editor to place. `kind::chrome` dresses a box as the spec's kinds do, and `kind::color` reads a JSON Canvas colour. `Kinds::with_fresh` names the node a double-click on empty canvas, `tab` on an empty one or pasted text makes, the text written through its kind's edit field.

Any node holds others through `canvas::contain`: a node names its container in `"container"`, or sits in the smallest node around it whose kind `holds`, as a group does. What a node holds, however deep, moves, copies and duplicates with it and paints above it, `drag::Drag::contents` carries it, and a node carried out of the container it names lets it go. `mindmap::carry` moves only what it is given, and `mindmap::node_at` takes which nodes are targets.
Groups hold what sits in their box, paint under it and are never drop targets, with the label drawn above the box and the frame washed in the group's colour.

`Kinds::with_root` finds files and group backgrounds under a directory, so image files preview and `background` and `backgroundStyle` paint. A link opens on a double-click, and a kind's `open` says what a double-click does in place of editing.

Edges are picked by a click, removed by `backspace` and labelled by a double-click or `f2`, and labels are drawn. A picked node shows side handles that drag out a connector — onto a node, or onto nothing to make one — and a corner that resizes it through `Change::Resize`, both ways; a text node pulled taller keeps the height as `"minHeight"` (`kind::min_height`) and still grows with its content. `CanvasEditor::selected_edge` and `select_edge`, `CanvasEvent::EdgeSelected` and `Canvas::edge` are new, and presets `3` and `5` paint yellow and cyan.

The canvas undoes and redoes: `cmd-z` and `cmd-shift-z`, or `CanvasEditor::undo` and `redo`, over every batch that landed through `submit` or `apply`, with an add and the typing into it as one step. `change::apply` answers the changes that undo it, and `apply_all` does a batch.

The selection is many: shift- or cmd-click gathers it, a shift-drag on empty canvas draws a marquee, `cmd-a` takes all and `escape` none. Removing, nudging, dragging, copying and duplicating act on all of it; `CanvasEditor::selected_nodes` and `set_selection` read and set it, and `drag::Drag::with` carries the rest of it.

`cmd-c`, `cmd-x`, `cmd-v` and `cmd-d` copy, cut, paste and duplicate as JSON Canvas through `canvas::clip`, minting fresh ids and hanging a pasted branch under the selection in a tree. Plain text pastes as a text node. A middle-button drag pans.

`canvas::layout` makes layout pluggable: a `Layout` is an `arrange` function and the `flow` its trees grow in. `MINDMAP`, `BALANCED` (a root's branches both ways), `DOWN` and `FREE` ship, and `mindmap::arrange` takes a `Flow`.

A kind says what its nodes let the reader do — `draggable`, `selectable`, `connectable`, `resizable`, `deletable` through `Kind::can(Capabilities)` — and a node or edge refuses one with a field of its own. Every command honours it, so a key, a toolbar and a gesture stop at the same place, and a node that cannot connect or resize paints no handle for it. `CanvasEditor::can`, `node_can` and `edge_can` ask.

An edge has a kind too, named by its own `type`: `EdgeKinds` and `CanvasView::with_edge_kinds`, with `edge::curve()` the spec's and `edge::line()` a straight one. A kind says where the edge runs, how thick it paints, how near a press picks it, what its label edits and what it lets the reader do. The geometry is pure in `canvas::path` — `Ends` in, a `Path` of quadratic segments out — so a press is measured against the line the paint draws.

A kind declares its handles: `Kind::handles` and `EdgeKind::handles` answer a `Handle` of an id, a `Spot` and a `Role`. A node's spots are its sides and its corner, an edge's are its ends and points along it; the roles are `Connect`, `Resize` and `Reconnect`. The canvas works out where each lands from the box or the path, a kind that declares none has none, and dragging an edge's end carries it onto another node. A connector writes down the handle it left from in `fromHandle` and leaves exactly where it sits, offset along the side and all, with `fromSide` still written for readers that know only the spec. `Capability::Reconnectable` says whether an edge may be carried.

`Options` is what the canvas is tuned by — zoom limits and step, the drag threshold, the nudge, the duplicate's offset, the undo steps kept, the smallest box a corner pulls to, `fit`'s padding, the snap's reach and the drift step — in place of constants no app could reach. `Style` measures the canvas's own paint, and `Overlays` replaces every mark the canvas makes beside the kinds: the ring, a drop's wash, a handle, the far-off placeholder, the grid and the guides. `CanvasView::with_options`, `with_style` and `with_overlays` take them, and the tools read the options too.

Arrows walk a tree the way its layout grows it (`mindmap::walk`), or go to the nearest node on a free canvas (`layout::nearest`). `shift`-arrows nudge the selection, and a double-click on empty canvas adds a node there.
changed: `CanvasEditor` is the canvas without a window — the document, its kinds and layout, the selection, history and the part in view, behind commands — and `CanvasView` paints one: `view.editor()` reads it and `view.update_editor(cx, |editor| …)` runs commands, announcing them as `CanvasEvent`s. `canvas`, `submit`, `apply`, `select`, `undo`, `fit`, `set_layout` and the rest move from the view to the editor; the view keeps `copy`, `cut` and `paste` through the clipboard. The change filter is `Fn(&Canvas, Change) -> Option<Change>`, without `App`.

Kinds belong to a view: `CanvasView::with_kinds` and `CanvasEditor::with_kinds`, with `set_kinds` naming them for views that name none. `Kind`'s `sizing`, `edit`, `child` and `holds` live in `Kind::rules`, and `kind::kind`, `holds` and `fresh` are `Kinds::get`, `holds` and `fresh`.
The selection is `Item`s, nodes or one edge: `CanvasEditor::selection` answers them and `selected_nodes` the node ids.

Every canvas names its layout — `CanvasView::new(doc, layout, cx)` — and there is no default. A `Layout` carries what its edits mean: `reach`, `walk`, `link`, `extend`, `paste_under`, `duplicate_under`, `pins` and the `drag` it moves with, filled by `Layout::free` or `Layout::tree`, so the view holds no tree branch of its own. `drag::moves` is a free canvas's drag, which pins nothing. `mindmap::arrange` and `roots` take which nodes frame others in place of matching `group` by name, and `mindmap::node_at` is `contain::topmost`, the one hit-test.

Each gesture is a `canvas::tool::Tool`: the view says what a press landed on (`Hit`) and the first tool to take it holds the pointer until it comes up. `tool::defaults()` — `Connect`, `Resize`, `Reconnect`, `PickEdge`, `Marquee`, `Create`, `Select`, `Pan` — are what `CanvasView::with_tools` replaces. A tool commands the editor, draws through a `Sketch` and asks the view for an editor through a `Wish`; `escape` gives up the gesture in hand.

`Kind` holds closures, so a kind carries what it needs: build one with `Kind::new(render)` and `sizing`, `edit`, `open`, `child` and `holds`, and a field with `Field::new`. The spec's kinds are `kind::text()`, `file()`, `link()`, `group()` and `unknown()` in place of the constants.

`CanvasEvent::Selected` carries the whole selection. `Change::AddNode` takes an `index`. `mindmap::reparent`, `detach` and `carry` take many ids, `carry` a distance rather than a place, and `node_at` skips many branches.

`with_layout`, `CanvasEditor::layout` and `set_layout` replace `with_arrange`, `arrange` and `set_arrange`, and `Arrange` is gone. `keys::SelectParent`, `SelectChild`, `SelectPrev` and `SelectNext` are `SelectLeft`, `SelectRight`, `SelectUp` and `SelectDown`.

`Change` is a graph's vocabulary — `AddNode`, `AddEdge`, `RemoveNodes`, `RemoveEdges`, `MoveNodes`, `Resize`, `UpdateNode`, `UpdateEdge` — and the editor lands them in batches: `submit` and `apply` take many, one refused change refuses the batch, and `CanvasEvent::Changed` carries a `Vec`. `change::added` finds the node a batch adds.

Tree edits answer batches: `mindmap::child` and `sibling` answer `Option<Vec<Change>>`, and `remove`, `reparent`, `detach`, `carry` and `unpin` are new. `drag` handlers answer the same, against the document the preview never touched.

A canvas's measured heights and its layout are announced by `CanvasEvent::Changed`, unfiltered, so a save on `Changed` writes what is shown. `mindmap::arrange` answers the moves without applying them.
fixed: A drag or resize in hand paints over the document rather than writing into it: `CanvasEditor::canvas` and a save stay as they were until the drop lands, and layout during a gesture is no longer announced.

`backspace` on a free canvas removes only the node, not everything its edges reach. An edge marked `"tree": false` is a cross link, never a branch, so it is not followed by layout, removal or the arrow keys.

summary: A pluggable mindmap canvas over JSON Canvas, scrollbar overlays for either axis, and line numbers in markdown source.
new: `bezel-canvas` is a mindmap canvas over JSON Canvas 1.0: pan, zoom, keyboard editing and editing in place, with the fields the spec does not name kept and written back. `CanvasView` is the surface; `model`, `mindmap`, `change` and `drag` are pure.

`canvas::set_kinds` gives each node `type` a `Kind`: how it renders, whether its box is `Fixed` or `Grows`, its `Chrome`, which field editing changes, and what `tab` makes under it. The spec's four ship as `kind::TEXT`, `FILE`, `LINK` and `GROUP`, and `canvas::text_style` scales type with the zoom.

Every canvas edit is a `Change`. `CanvasView::with_changes` sees each before it lands and can refuse or rewrite it, `submit` sends an app's own through the same filter, and `CanvasEvent::Changed` carries what landed.

`CanvasView::with_drag` picks what dropping a node does — `drag::pin`, `reparent`, `detach`, or an app's own. A held node previews its drop: a ring on the new parent, the connector it would make, the ones it would cut. Nodes a layout moves glide there over the new `motion::LAYOUT`.

`scroll::Overlay` is a stateful scrollbar for either axis, laid over its pane `BAR_INSET` from the edges, and `scroll::Viewport` is a scroll container that owns its handle and overlay. `scroll::set_visibility` picks `Scrolling`, `Always` or `Never` for every default overlay, markdown code blocks and tables included.

The markdown source view numbers its lines, and the gutter widens when the count gains a digit. `markdown::set_source_style` returns a `SourceStyle` per theme for the minimum digits, the gap and the colour, or turns the numbers off.

summary: A pane scrolls under a drag held at its edge, and the editor and terminal resize live.
new: `scroll::drift` scrolls a pane while a drag is held near its edge, faster the closer the pointer and full speed past it. Feed it from a typed `on_drag_move` with `DriftState::aim`; `drift_velocity` is the ramp on its own.

`Editor::set_text_size` changes the base size of an open editor without rebuilding the document, clearing undo or dropping the zoom. `TerminalElement::with_text_size` sets the grid's font size, with the line height scaled to match.
`appearance::keep_background` leaves a window's background alone across appearance switches, for a window that is opaque on purpose.
fixed: Switching back to `AppearanceMode::System` resolves to what the OS says rather than the mode just left. A pinned mode's override was being recorded as the system appearance.
The window that observed an appearance change gets the new background too. It was mid-update when the reapply ran, so it was skipped.

summary: A sheet can come up from the bottom, a drag holds its run past the edge of the box, and a doc page is the component and its signatures.
new: `popover::Side::Bottom` pins a sheet to the bottom edge — full width, up over `DIALOG_IN` and back down over `MENU_OUT`, on the same scrim and the same exit clock as the side panels. It is what a narrow window wants instead of a side panel that leaves the page behind it no room. The rounding and the hairline follow the edge, so the corners left square are the two against the window.
changed: `popover::sheet` takes an `extent` where it took a `width`. The side decides which axis it is read along — a width on `Left` and `Right`, a height on `Bottom` — while the other always spans the viewport, so the old name would have been wrong exactly half the time.

Every page under `/docs` is the component, one usage block, and the API as real Rust: each signature inside the `trait` or `impl` that declares it, with `// ...` wherever the block is a selection rather than the whole item, and the crate's docs.rs beside the source link for the rest. The prose that used to argue for each design is gone — what a reader needed from it was the signature. 21,600 words to 5,000, and the pages that kept a table kept one because its rows are data rather than Rust: the markdown spellings, the glass measurements, the feature gates.

A gallery section is a list of named examples rather than one undivided page. `?s=<section>&e=<example>` embeds one, and a doc page moves a single embed between them as the reader scrolls — which is what keeps one 14MB wasm instance on a page rather than one per snippet. The catalog declares the keys and a test asserts the page paints exactly those, so an `example=` that points at nothing fails the build instead of showing the wrong demo.
fixed: A drag that leaves a text field keeps carrying the run. `on_mouse_move` on the field's own box fires only while the box is the thing under the pointer, so a selection dragged past the edge froze at the last character inside it — and the last line of a full box was unreachable, since reaching it means passing the edge. The move comes off the window now, which arrives wherever the pointer went.

A field hit tests at its own line height rather than the window's. Outside the field's own paint there is no text style on the stack, so a click handler was told the window's default and walked the rows at the wrong stride: the caret landed a line or two above the pointer, further out the lower you clicked, until the last lines of a full box could not be reached at all. `TextField::offset_bounds` loses its `window` argument with it.

summary: A document and the markdown it would save are the same view now, and an app spells marks CommonMark never named.
new: `Mode::Source` swaps a document for its markdown in the same editor, with the same focus and the same undo history. `toggle_source` flips, `mode()` reads, `with_mode` opens on one, and `EditorEvent::ModeChanged` is how a host's own trigger hears about a switch it did not make — an undo across one, for instance. The caret crosses: going in the offset is exact through markers, escapes and marks, because it is the serializer that places it; coming back it lands in the block and the word it was in. The source is one editable text, so the block chrome stays out of it, and `source()` answers with the markdown in either mode — a save needs no branch.

`markdown::source_spans` colours markdown *source* — headings, emphasis, fences, link destinations — without a grammar and without tree-sitter, which is what lets a source view have colour in a browser build. A fence tagged `md` takes it wherever the installed highlighter has no answer, so the editor's source mode is coloured with nothing installed at all. `serialize_at` and `parse_at` are the pair the caret crosses on, each placing a sentinel and reading off where it came out, so neither can drift from the serializer or the parser it rides on.

`markdown::Marks` is the dialect an app spells itself. `Mark` stays closed — bold, italic, strike, code, links — because every one of those has a spelling CommonMark already reads; underline, highlight and a colour do not, so an app registers a name and the delimiter for it and `parse_with`/`serialize_with` take it from there. `set_marks` is the gpui-side half the editing surface reads, `set_mark_paint` says what each name looks like, and `Editor::with_marks` gives one editor a dialect rather than the installed one. A registered delimiter is lifted out before CommonMark sees the source, which is what keeps `\=\=` an escape and the fixed point a fixed point; a name nothing paints round trips and reads as the text it wraps.

`Editor::formatting()` is a toolbar's whole state in one read: the marks that are lit, the caret's block label, whether `cmd-E` would fence rather than span, and the mode. Four reaches into the document before, and a bar answering half its questions from this frame and half from the last lights the wrong button for a frame. `marks` is what a button *means* — what the whole selection carries, or at a collapsed caret what the next character typed would, so it stays lit between `cmd-B` and the letter that spends it. `editor::turns()` is the block vocabulary the slash menu and the gutter handle already offer, so a dropdown of your own cannot drift from the two bezel opens.

`editor::Chrome` turns the editor's own affordances off one at a time — the gutter handle, the slash menu, a fence's language picker, the menu a pasted URL drops — for an app putting its own in the same place. All of them are on until it says otherwise. `layouts()` hands out where everything landed last frame, blocks, pictures, the language label, and `rects(selection)` for the painted rows of a range; `editor::keys` is the whole action set, for an app binding chords of its own.

A long line in a fence wraps. It is the default because the caret is what reads a fence in an editor and a sideways scroller can hold it off the right edge with nothing on the page to bring it back; `markdown::set_layout(cx, Layout { wrap_code: false })` asks for the scroller instead. A wrapped line is rows of one layout, exactly as a paragraph already is, so the hit test costs nothing.

A menu row's description keeps to one line and hovers for the rest. `Item::with_long_description` sets both from one string, since a sentence that needs clipping is one no caller should write twice, and `with_tooltip` sets the hover text alone — which is also how a disabled row says why it is disabled. One described row widens the panel the way one icon opens the glyph gutter.

Pictures copied in a file manager paste. A clipboard carrying a file carries its path as text beside the path itself, so the paste reads the pictures first and the text only when there are none — the same order a screenshot and its file name already took.

`/docs/markdown` is the dialect written down: every block and mark, the prefixes that type them, and what a flat document does with nesting, each row spelling on the left and result on the right. `/docs/ribbon` is a docked formatting bar built entirely from `formatting()` and `turns()`, with no library code behind it — `apps/gallery/src/patterns/ribbon.rs` to copy.
changed: `ImageStore` is a struct of `fn` fields rather than one function. `keep` is handed the `Entity<Editor>` doing the asking and the `&App`, because a store needs state — which article is open, where the vault is — and in gpui that state lives in the app rather than in a capture; an app with two windows open has two answers and a bare call could not tell them apart. `accepts` is the second field, for a build whose idea of a picture is not the extension guess. `Default` means the next field is not a break.

`LinkPreview` takes `&App`. A preview's cache lives in the app, so the old bare call had to reach for a `static` to read its own. Shared rather than exclusive because this is asked at paint: the fetch a `None` implies belongs to whatever notices it, not to the paint that returned it.

`Brand::vibrancy` is a three-valued `Vibrancy` rather than a bool, resolved against the appearance on every install. The honest answer depends on the appearance and the appearance moves under the app — the OS switches at sunset — so a bool had to be rewritten by whoever noticed, and nothing outside `theme` is told when a palette is installed. `Auto` frosts where the palette is built for it, which is dark alone; `On` is for an app that has tuned a light palette to carry one; `Off` is what a Reduce-transparency switch sets. The vibrancy tint is left where the brand put it even when the window is opaque, so turning the frost back on returns the coverage the app tuned.
fixed: A link destination with a space in it survives being written. `![a](/My Notes/a.png)` ended at the space and the rest became text, which is what a picture dragged in from a folder with a space in its name did to a document on the next save. Destinations are written bare wherever that reads back as the URL handed in and in angles where it would not — whitespace, a backslash, an unbalanced `)` — with control characters percent-encoded, since neither spelling can hold one.

summary: An icon is a value now — `Icon` — and `theme.icon` paints one from the ladder and the palette.
new: `icons::Icon` is what a component takes, and it erases where the drawing came from: a glyph compiled in, `Icon::asset(..)` out of the app's own `AssetSource`, or `Icon::file(..)` off disk. Every icon-taking signature moves to `impl Into<Icon>`, so a constant still passes as itself and an app can finally paint art the set does not carry. SwiftUI's `Image` erases its sources the same way.

`theme.icon(..)` and `theme.icon_at(role, ..)` paint an icon at a rung of the type ladder in the palette's text tone. Both are defaults a `Styled` call after them overrides, which is how a component keeps its own metric — what they buy is the floor: gpui resolves an svg's tone from that element's own style and never inherits one, so an icon with nothing set paints *nothing*. It is a catalog trait like the rest, `use ui::widgets::Icons`.

`Icon::solid` is the filled variant as a property of the value rather than a second call — SwiftUI's `.symbolVariant(.fill)`. `icons::solid(..)` stays for the common case, and the filled document is now rewritten once per glyph and kept rather than rebuilt on every frame a solid icon is on screen.
`bezel-icons` publishes a README of its own: the features, the names, and how the pinned-release upgrade works.
fixed: A menu row's leading glyph painted nothing. `menu` was the one component the icon port left holding an asset path, and bezel registers no asset source, so the gutter opened and stayed empty. The demo menus carry glyphs now, which is what would have shown it.

summary: The icon set becomes the whole of Lucide, ported from a pinned release and named the way Lucide names it.
new: Every Lucide icon is in the set — 1834 of them, ported by `crates/icons/build.rs` from a pinned release rather than picked by hand. Modules are Lucide's categories and constants are Lucide's names, so `arrows::ArrowBigDown` is what lucide.dev calls `arrow-big-down` and nothing has to be looked up twice. One cargo feature per category, none on by default, `full` for all 42 — and `ui` needs three, which are the floor for anything depending on it.

`icons::solid` paints a glyph filled, for the weight Lucide does not draw. Filled *and* stroked, so the outer edge lands exactly where `icons::icon` puts it and a control swapping between them does not jump.
changed: An icon constant is the SVG itself rather than a path into an asset source. The linker drops whatever a binary never names, which is finer than any feature can be, and an app registers nothing: `icons::Assets` is gone and so is the `with_assets` call that carried it. `icons::icon` takes the constant.

Icon names are Lucide's, in Lucide's own casing: `system::MAGNIFER` is `glyph::Search`, and the `_BOLD` twins are `icons::solid(glyph::Play)`. The set no longer names a glyph twice, so there is no mapping left to drift.

The assets and the module tree are generated and gitignored, and bundled into the published crate. A consumer never runs the download, and the crate still builds offline, under `cargo vendor` and on docs.rs.
Moves to bezel-gpui 0.3.10. `ContentMask` carries `corner_radii` now; `ContentMask::new(bounds)` is the plain rectangle every mask was before it.
fixed: 22 of the 84 icons the set used to carry had drifted from Lucide — `play` was still the sharp triangle Lucide retired, and `trash-2` no longer exists upstream at all. The set was pinned to a snapshot of a re-encoding crate that stopped at 1599 glyphs and never moved; porting from a release is what keeps that from recurring, since bumping the pinned version shows every redrawn glyph as a diff.

A code block keeps a sideways scroll to itself. gpui hands a vertical scroller the horizontal delta whenever its own axis reads zero, and its scroll handling never stops the event, so panning a fence drove the page down behind it. Wide tables carried the same bug.

A code block scrolls to the end of its longest line. Its horizontal padding sat on the scroller rather than in the content, and a scroll container's trailing padding is not part of what it will scroll to, so the last characters of a long line stayed behind the right edge with nowhere left to go.

summary: Menus nest the way SwiftUI's do, prose selects with no editor behind it, and a nested surface keeps its own press and wheel.
new: A menu row can drop a menu of its own. `menu::Item::submenu` nests exactly as a SwiftUI `Menu` does, and `menu::card` paints the panels itself — a chevron marks the row, hover or `right` opens it, `left` and `escape` close one level at a time. A submenu with nothing selectable in it is a dead end, so the keyboard steps over it like any other dead row.

`markdown::selectable` gives prose a selection with no editor behind it. The renderer already painted a `Selection` and the layouts already turned a point back into a `Cursor`; what was missing was the gesture. `selectable::copied` returns what a reader dragged over as plain text — the words, not the markup under them.
`skills/bezel` and `skills/bezel-contributing` ship in the repo: what an agent needs to write a bezel call, and what a change to bezel has to land with.

`popover::menu_trigger` wires a trigger to the popup it toggles, so the press/release split cannot be got wrong. `on_mouse_down_out` fires on the press and `on_click` on the release, which no click handler can tell apart — the note has to be taken in the phase the dismissal cannot precede, and now the library takes it. `popover::dismiss_on_out` is the card half, `popover::trigger_press` the press half alone for a trigger whose open is more than `Popup::open`, and `popover::close_popup` the `begin_close` + `reap_popup` pair every dismissal owed.

`scroll::claim_wheel` lets a nested pane keep the wheel it can act on. gpui's scroll listener neither stops propagation nor asks whether an ancestor scrolls too, so an output box inside a transcript scrolled itself and dragged the transcript with it — every scrolling pane under the pointer moved at once. It asks whether the pane moved rather than whether it had room to, which is the same answer one notch too late: the notch that lands exactly on the end would finish the pane's travel and jump the page behind it. Chained at the ends, so a short inner list does not strand the wheel and make the pointer move, and a pane whose content fits never claims anything.

`menu::Item::with_description` gives an action row a second line — what a command will do, which file it will act on, for a row whose name does not say enough on its own. One described row widens the panel, the way one icon opens the glyph gutter, because a description is a sentence rather than a name.
changed: A menu's pointer and keyboard share one cursor. Hovering a row moves the selection rather than lighting a row of its own, so an open submenu can only ever hang off the row that is live. Hovering now shows the selection tone rather than the softer wash it used to.

`menu::card` reports what the pointer did as a `Hit`, dismissal included. A card sees only its own bounds, so with a submenu open a click on one of its rows read as a click away; every panel now reports the press it did not contain, and the press none of them contained is the one that dismisses.
`MenubarEvent::Selected` carries a path rather than a row index — one index per level, outermost first, which `Menu::at` turns back into the item.

`Item`'s builders rewrite the row in place rather than taking it apart and putting it back together field by field. Threading a new field through five rebuilds is how a field gets dropped from one of them.
fixed: The editor's block and language menus stay shut when their trigger is pressed a second time. A card's out-click fires on the press and a trigger's click on the release, so without a note taken on the way down the press closed the menu and the release opened it straight back up. Both menus also play their exit now instead of vanishing.

The combobox, the date picker and the gallery's select each carried their own copy of the press note; they share one now. It is taken in the capture phase rather than on bubble, so it no longer depends on a dismissal reaching for `Popup::begin_close` over `Popup::close`.

summary: The editor takes tab for itself, and the document is sized apart from the app around it.
new: A document carries its own text size, with chords to adjust it — so the prose can be set larger without the chrome following it.
fixed: Tab indents a list item in an editor that sits inside focus traversal, which had been taking the key to move focus instead.
The block handle moves in with an indented block, and a nested run restarts its numbering rather than continuing the run above it.

summary: The icon set moves into a crate of its own, declared from Lucide rather than checked in.
new: `bezel-icons` is its own crate. The set is declared from Lucide and generated at build time, so no SVG is stored in git and a consumer picks the categories it paints with.
changed: The default font is the system face the type ladder was measured on, rather than one the ladder never described.
fixed: The container owns the gap above a group box, so two stacked boxes no longer carry a doubled one between them.

summary: Glass renders over a vibrant window, and the chrome's transparency stops being the window's.
new: `menu::card` is shared: the panel the menubar drops is the same one any caller can paint a list of rows into.
A scroll pane can mark its items on a rail beside it — where you are in a long list, without a scrollbar's worth of chrome.
`apps/parity` draws one scene twice, in bezel and in AppKit side by side, which is how the measurements stay honest.
changed: A window's transparency is split from its chrome's, so glass renders over a vibrant window instead of compositing against the wrong thing underneath.
Every hover and selection runs off one pair of tokens, rather than each component picking a tone that nearly matched.
fixed: A surface clamps its corners to the box it actually paints, so a small element cannot round itself away.
A row title clips instead of ellipsising, the group box row matches macOS metrics, every type role gets its measured line height, and every control sizes off its measured line box.

summary: Every surface is measured frost or glass, every text size sits on a measured ladder, and an app can paint a fenced block itself.
new: A type ladder behind every text size: each role is a measurement with a note saying where it was read, rather than a number somebody liked.
Comments anchor to ranges that survive editing, so an annotation stays on the words it was about after the text around it moves.
An app can paint a fenced block itself, and `bezel-blocks` ships the painted ones — one feature per block, so nothing you do not render is compiled.
Icon buttons and grouped buttons, a ghost control frame, and a memory row on the stats meter.
changed: Glass is rebuilt from measurements of a real `NSGlassEffectView` rather than from an approximation of one.
The space ladder is replaced by the measured system gap — one number the platform names, instead of a scale invented around it.
A field's type and the editor's text inset are configurable, and the gallery lays out on narrow windows.
The architecture notes are folded into a compact `CONTRIBUTING`.
fixed: A menu has one cursor and marks the chosen row, instead of lighting the hovered row and the selected row at once.
The caret, the gutter handle and block deletion in the editor; a block is kept in an empty document; the handle centres on its first row; an embed card hugs its text and rounds its cover.

summary: Meet the liquid glass — and a window that stops animating when nobody is looking at it.
new: Liquid glass, and the lens brought to the web build alongside it.
changed: Animation stops while the app is in the background. A spinner nobody can see still costs a frame at the display's rate, for as long as it stays mounted.
A split handle can skip its own divider, for a pane that draws one of its own.
fixed: The focus ring has its own hairline token rather than borrowing a border's.
The stats meter shows on the page that documents it.

summary: One leased clock behind every animation, and a meter that shows what a still window costs.
new: A floating frame with a CPU and GPU meter, and a draggable floating panel to hang either off.
gpui's frame overlay cycles behind a profiler flag, so the cost of a frame is visible without a second tool.
Pixel mascots for list rows.
changed: Every animation drive is merged onto one leased clock, and every frame request routes through `Painter`. An element asking for frames used to ask on behalf of the whole window.
Components notify the view rather than refreshing the window, so a repaint costs the subtree that changed instead of all of it.
The gallery floats its content card over a bare rail.
fixed: Checklists are no longer rewritten on save, which had been turning a document into a diff against itself.

summary: Brand — the palette an app builds its own theme from, made from the gallery's Create page.
new: `Brand`, and the gallery's Create page that produces one: pick a palette and the snippet to paste comes out the other side.
Images resize in the block editor, and a width is spelled in the markdown itself as `![alt|480](url)`.
The navigation rail floats under the traffic lights instead of starting below them.
changed: The frost alpha is a `Brand` knob rather than a constant every app inherits.
fixed: A slider drag stays with the slider it started on, and the slider takes the pointer cursor.
A horizontal scroller locks to the gesture's axis instead of drifting on a diagonal.

summary: bezel 0.1.0 on crates.io — `bezel-*` packages with short lib names, and docs served as markdown for agents.
new: Published to crates.io. The packages are `bezel-*` and the libs are short, so a consumer writes `ui::` and `theme::` rather than the package name twice.
Images in the block editor, the nav row, and the window titlebar strip.
The docs are served as markdown as well as HTML, which is what an agent reads.
fixed: Mobile overflow on the site, and the keyboard opening on every preview tap.

summary: The library itself: the components, the gallery that documents them, the markdown model, the block editor, and the site they all ship to.
new: The component set — real backdrop-blur glass, editable text fields that wrap and scroll, form controls, a command palette, combobox, hover card, sheet, resizable split, follow scroll and a step row.
The gallery: a docs browser with a top nav, a page per component, and an element inspector on `cmd-alt-i`.
`bezel`, the facade crate, and `apps/hello`, the worked example the README walks through.
A block document model that round-trips markdown to a fixed point, and a Notion-style block editor over it in a crate of its own.
tree-sitter syntax highlighting for fenced code, a terminal emulator and grid view, and the agent crate with thinking orbs and generated blob avatars.
The docs site, with the gallery compiled to wasm and running in the page.
changed: Components are catalog traits on `Theme` via `ThemeExt`: stateless paint hangs off the environment, and a caller overrides by chaining gpui modifiers on what comes back.
One button with three shipped styles, rather than a button per style. A closed enum picks between them; radius, colour and padding never become parameters.
Hover is caller-owned, so a component cannot install a listener the caller then needs for something else.

summary: The bezel holds the glass.
new: The first commit.
